$comment: Root ADR-0145: a region code change (old code -> new code) is stored in one place, and a parcel pair (old PNU -> new PNU) in one other; everything else derives from them or is retired. scripts/guard/region-code-pairs-have-one-home.sh reads this file and refuses (1) a lakehouse table, other than the home and the derived tables named here with a reason, whose columns have a pair shape below, (2) code that names a retired holder outside the paths listed for it, (3) a retired path that exists again. Markdown is prose and is not read; machine-read files under docs directories (the pipeline graph JSON, say) are code and are. The guard reads the names from here and nowhere else, so prose elsewhere cannot trip it and a new holder is added in this file, not in the guard.

derived_tables.gold.place_id_changelog: ADR-0113 §8 release changelog: which place id changed code between two ID releases. Rebuilt from the ID registry every release, never read back as a source of pairs; ADR-0145 leaves the place-id tables as they are.

retired.name: reference.legal_dong_code
retired.why: ADR-0103 time dictionary. No reader, never created in production; the change table and its snapshot source replace it.

retired.name: reference.sigungu_canonical_crosswalk
retired.why: Stored 시군구 crosswalk with two writers and the opposite direction. The crosswalk is a view of the change table; its file form is the projection.

retired.name: catalog.administrative_unit_transition
retired.why: ADR-0105 transition table, never produced. Not produced until a consumer exists, then as a view of the change table. Its migration, grant, the publication ledger's reference, the schema tests and the pipeline graph (which must list every table a migration declares, scripts/catalog/pipeline_graph.py) may name it; nothing may write it.
